You can now use Gemini in Google Slides to edit multiple slides or an entire presentation at once. With a single prompt in the Slides side panel, you can update content throughout a deck, refresh visual styles in bulk, or match the style of another presentation. Gemini determines which slides need to change and applies edits directly to your native, editable slides, so you stay in full control to make any further adjustments.
Try the following to update your presentations in less time:


Refresh visual styles: Update fonts, backgrounds, color schemes, and more across the entire deck. For example: "Update this whole deck to match the style of this [reference file]"
Update content throughout the deck: Simplify, expand, or change the focus of your presentation, grounded in your files from Google Drive. For example: "Update this presentation to include more details based on [reference file]."
Combine or expand slides: Condense multiple slides into one, or add new slides to an existing deck. For example: "Summarize slides 5–7 into a single slide."
Make styling consistent: Align title styles or remove page numbers across all slides. For example: "Make the titles on all slides the same font size and color."


Once Gemini finishes, a summary of the changes appears in the side panel. Edits are applied as if you made them, so you can use undo or version history to review or revert them.
Note: At launch, this feature will be supported in English only.

# Gemini in Google Slides Can Now Edit a Whole Presentation at Once

> **In short:** Google says Gemini in Google Slides can now change several slides, or an entire deck, from a single prompt in the side panel. It can restyle fonts and colors, rewrite content using your Google Drive files, merge slides, and make formatting consistent. Every change can be undone, and the feature launches in English only.

Think about the last time you had to fix the same thing on fifteen slides: a font that was slightly wrong, a title that was a size too big, a page number you didn't want. It's tedious work. Google's new option lets you describe the change once and let Gemini, the company's AI assistant, handle the repetition.

## What the feature actually does

According to Google, you can use Gemini on one slide, several slides, or the whole presentation. Gemini works out which slides need to change, then edits your existing slides directly. The result stays native and editable, so you can still click into any text box or shape and adjust it yourself.

Google lists four main ways to use it:

- **Refresh the visual style.** Update fonts, backgrounds, and color schemes across the deck. For example: "Update this whole deck to match the style of this [reference file]."
- **Update the content.** Simplify, expand, or shift the focus of your presentation, based on files stored in Google Drive. For example: "Update this presentation to include more details based on [reference file]."
- **Combine or add slides.** Merge several slides into one, or add new slides. For example: "Summarize slides 5–7 into a single slide."
- **Make the styling consistent.** Align title styles or remove page numbers everywhere. For example: "Make the titles on all slides the same font size and color."

A prompt, in case the word is new, is simply the instruction you type to an AI. The clearer it names the slides and the change, the more likely the result is what you wanted.

## Checking and undoing the changes

When Gemini finishes, a summary of what it changed appears in the side panel. Google says the edits are applied as if you had made them by hand. That means the normal safety net applies: you can use undo, or look through version history to review or revert the changes.

Before you accept a big edit, it's worth clicking through a few slides. Spot-check the first, the middle, and the last one. If something looks off, revert and try a narrower prompt, such as naming a single slide range.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** If you prepare slides for a family reunion, a school club, or a community meeting, you can ask for one consistent look instead of fixing each slide by hand.
- **For your business or work:** If you update the same deck for different clients or audiences, you can point Gemini at a reference file and ask it to match that style, then adjust the details yourself.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a small, low-risk request, like "Make the titles on all slides the same font size and color." Check the result, then try something bigger.
- **If you already use it:** Combine steps in one prompt, such as asking Gemini to restyle the deck to match a reference file and then remove page numbers. Review the side panel summary before you move on.

Google notes that the feature supports English only at launch, so keep your prompts and content in English for now.

## Wrap-up

Gemini in Google Slides is designed to take the repetitive parts of editing off your hands: restyling, tidying titles, and condensing slides, all from one prompt. You stay in charge, because every edit can be reviewed or undone. Your next step: open a deck you already have, pick one small change you keep repeating, and write it as a single prompt, naming the slides it should affect.
